highlights.title: What happens when neutrinos swap identities inside a supernova?
highlights.summary: Our basic understanding of core-collapse supernovae hasn't changed in decades. Large stars burn through all the fuel at their cores and start creating heavier elements in reactions that consume energy.
body: And, generally, that's right. But there's an entire busload of devils in the details. The statistics of supernovae that we've observed indicate that the model may be seriously incomplete. And on the theoretical side, there are still plenty of uncertainties, including over some of the basics, such as whether all core collapses actually result in a supernova.

A paper being released by Physical Review D provides what might be a potential explanation for the discrepancy: flavor-changing neutrinos. Neutrinos play a key role in our current models of supernovae, and right now, those models don't take into account one of neutrinos' most striking features: their ability to change identity.
points: Our basic understanding of core-collapse supernovae hasn't changed in decades.
Large stars burn through all the fuel at their cores and start creating heavier elements in reactions that consume energy.
But there's an entire busload of devils in the details.

highlights.title: Helping older adults use AI in everyday life
highlights.summary: OpenAI and AARP are bringing free, hands-on ChatGPT workshops to 1,000 older adults across 10 U.S. cities to build practical AI skills safely.
body: AI should be useful and accessible to everyone. That means making sure people of every age have the support they need to use these tools to help make everyday life easier. For older adults, that can mean getting help planning a trip, understanding a confusing letter or bill, spotting a possible scam, pursuing a new hobby, or staying connected with family and loved ones.

Today, OpenAI Academy, in collaboration with Older Adults Technology Services (OATS) from AARP is hosting the Older Adults AI Skills Jam: a free, in-person learning experience designed to help older adults use ChatGPT confidently and safely. The Jam is part of a multi-year effort OpenAI launched with OATS to help older adults build practical AI skills and stay safe online through its flagship program, Senior Planet.

Data shows that older adults are increasingly using ChatGPT for practical guidance, finding information, and writing. In the U.S., the share of messages associated with people 55+ grew from 6% to nearly 10% in a year.

highlights.title: F1 announce 2027 calendar and increase in Sprint rounds
highlights.summary: Formula 1 has announced its 2027 calendar and an increase in the number of Sprint weekends from six to 10, with the season starting in Bahrain.
body: For a fourth consecutive year, there are 24 rounds scheduled with Portugal's Portimao and Turkey's Istanbul Park returning to the calendar.

As expected, the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort falls off the schedule while the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya moves into a rotational deal with Spa-Francorchamps that will see the Spanish event held in even numbered years from 2028 and the Belgian Grand Prix held in odd numbered years from 2027.

F1 had delayed its calendar announcement for next year due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which has created uncertainty over the end of the current season with Qatar and Abu Dhabi still currently scheduled to take place later this year.
Bahrain will host a four-day pre-season test on February 24-27 before holding the 2027 season-opener on March 12-14 and it will be a Sprint weekend, with the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix a week later.

body: Laika specializes in stop-motion animation. It is best known for the 2009 creepy-cute classic Coraline, but nearly all of its movies have been very well received. As for feature-length films, the studio followed up Coraline with ParaNorman (2012), The Boxtrolls (2014), Kubo and the Two Strings (2016), and Missing Link (2019). Wildwood is set for release on Oct. 23, 2026.

Travis Knight is directing the film, having previously helmed Kubo and the Two Strings. Chris Butler wrote the screenplay, which is based on Colin Meloy and Carson Ellis’ fantasy novel of the same name. Caleb Deschanel is the cinematographer, and Dario Marianelli handles the music.

The movie stars Peyton Elizabeth Lee ( Andi Mac k) as Prue McKeel, the teenager out to rescue her little brother Mac. Carey Mulligan plays Alexandra, the film’s antagonist. It also features performances from Jacob Tremblay ( Room, Luca ), Mahershala Ali, Awkwafina, Angela Bassett, and more.

highlights.title: ‘Closing Night’ Review: Sarah Paulson and Naomi Watts Are Warring Sisters in Cody Fern’s Deliciously Histrionic Melodrama
highlights.summary: Toward the end of the deep-feeling, deliciously histrionic drama “Closing Night,” the film shifts tone. The first two acts — a whirlwind of long-deferred confrontations and fiery disclosures — lean on lively dark comedy as a pair of warring sisters explode with decades of rage and resentment.
body: The powerhouse actresses play fragile women navigating a devastating diagnosis in this darkly comic story about the secrets that bind us.

When the film begins, Sandra has extended an olive branch to April and Diane by inviting them to New York to see her perform on Broadway. Diane refuses, but April hesitantly makes the trip, only to learn that Theo — an artistic dilettante who lives in the city with his girlfriend, Lucy (Odessa A’zion) — has been lunching with Sandra behind her back. April receives the news as a betrayal. But Theo, long kept in the dark about his mom and aunt’s rupture, sees the meetings as a chance to get to know the famous relative who was, until then, a stranger.

highlights.title: Jess Cartner-Morley on fashion: pair a little skirt with a chunky jumper for the perfect balancing act
highlights.summary: Let your legs enjoy the last of the summer’s breeze while a thick top or jacket keeps away the autumn chill. This is the most enjoyable time of the year to get dressed because clothes can just be clothes.
body: And this benign early part of autumn is more fun to dress for than the equivalent weather in spring, because we still have a bit of summer swagger. The summer habit of wearing shorts and halter tops and even swimwear has gotten us a little loose, a little more laid-back about flashing a bit of skin here or there. It is about more than bare flesh, though. There is something about summer that flexes the flashy dresser in everyone – whether that’s fancy dress for a festival, or just the way that putting on a pair of sunglasses brings out your inner movie star.

It is very important to hold on to that summer glow, that more fabulous version of yourself, the one who starred in your holiday snaps carousel, for as long as you can. I do this literally, getting through my bodyweight in Dove Visible Glow, my preferred slap-it-on-like-body-lotion gradual self-tan, between now and when the clocks go back. But the less literal-minded among you can hold on to that lovely golden-hour feeling in your mind, as well as in your body. Stay locked into your summer playlist and keep hold of that windows-down, shades-on spirit of freedom at least until the leaves start to turn.

highlights.title: macOS 27 Golden Gate: The Ars Technica review
highlights.summary: Apple Intelligence is back, baby! That's right: Two years after its initial launch, Apple is giving its generative AI features their first significant upgrade, along with a new version of Siri that the company has been strongly insinuating would be a part of each of the last two macOS releases…
body: Generative AI is unavoidable if you install macOS 27 Golden Gate. I’m being very literal: There used to be a toggle you could hit if you wanted to turn off Apple Intelligence and delete the gigabytes’ worth of AI models it would download to your disk, and now there isn’t. Apple Intelligence defines the Golden Gate release, in everything from its marketing to its features to the chips it runs on to the amount of space it takes on your disk. Ready or not, here it is.

But if you can manage to look past that fanfare somehow, the operating system underneath Apple Intelligence is getting the kind of update that macOS users usually proclaim to like. Golden Gate addresses the most irritating of macOS 26 Tahoe’s design sins, adds a big pile of incremental improvements, and promises a bunch of under-the-hood fit-and-finish optimizations to make common tasks feel just a little faster and more reliable than before.

This makes for a combination that is occasionally jarring: big, hard-to-ignore and impossible-to-disable AI changes wedded to an understated update that in other years might have been called a “ Snow Leopard release.”

highlights.title: New AI technique could make minimally invasive surgeries safer and more precise
highlights.summary: This patient-specific method, called xvr, helps doctors use X-rays for surgical navigation in fields such as orthopedics and neurosurgery.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. You may not alter the images provided, other than to crop them to size. A credit line must be used when reproducing images; if one is not provided below, credit the images to "MIT."

Researchers created a new technique that accurately and rapidly matches X-rays captured during surgery with a patient’s preoperative 3D medical scan. This method could make it easier for clinicians to precisely pilot minimally invasive surgical tools, leading to faster and safer procedures.

Clinicians perform many minimally invasive surgeries using real-time X-rays to help them steer devices like catheters and endoscopes through tiny incisions. But since X-rays are flat images, it can be challenging to determine exactly where surgical tools are located and oriented within the patient’s body, increasing the risk of complications.

highlights.title: Arsenal? Chelsea? Man City? Which club has most valuable teens?
highlights.summary: The Premier League's teenage sensations are making headlines after Max Dowman's starring display for Arsenal and JJ Gabriel's revelation that he wants to leave Manchester United.
body: Dowman, 16, scored twice in Arsenal's Carabao Cup win over Ipswich, only hours after 15-year-old Gabriel had stunned Manchester United with his request to cancel his registration at the club.
Dowman's breakthrough and Gabriel's desire for first-team opportunities show how the stars of tomorrow are starting younger, but which Premier League clubs have the most valuable teens?

For this week's Between the Lines, we use Transfermarkt valuations to rank Premier League clubs by teenage value, albeit with the caveat that Transfermarkt does not assign valuations to young players with no first-team experience such as Gabriel.
According to Transfermarkt, Manchester City have the most valuable teenagers at a combined £122.6m, putting them just ahead of Chelsea on £121m, and Arsenal in third on £102.4m.

highlights.title: ‘Diablo 4’ Is Completely Free to Play On Steam for a Limited Time
highlights.summary: It's a great time to slay demons: coming off BlizzCon, Diablo 4 is free to try on Steam until Sept. 21. The base version is also 75% off on Steam and the Blizzard Store, at $12.49. Loot grinding awaits.
body: Still, Diablo 4’s free-to-play week comes with a few major caveats. Apparently, this version of the game restricts players to a maximum level of 30. As one Steam review noted, “After 2.4 hours I reached lvl. 16 and then, after completing a quest, got boosted to 30 instantly and got kicked off the character.” Diablo 4 is also free to try on Battle.net, letting you play the expansion class Spiritborn up to level 25.

Since its release on Oct. 17, 2023, Diablo 4 has had a somewhat complicated reception. While critics praised the game for its sharp art direction and fun combat, many players were put off by its always-online requirements. The base game currently has 73% positive user reviews on Steam, but its most recent reviews have fallen to 62%, seemingly due to backlash over how Blizzard has handled its DLC. Many character abilities are locked behind the Lord of Hatred DLC, which costs a comparable price to the full game. While the game and both DLCs are bundled together at $69.99, there isn’t a discount for those who already bought the base game.

highlights.summary: A brush with mortality inspired sisters Sophia and Camilla Minden to create a death-themed event featuring live bands, wild swimming … and an ‘emoshpit’ Raised in the Lake District on “music, moss and macaroni cheese,” Sophia and Camilla Minden were mindful of death from a very early age.
body: What they didn’t expect was that little more than a decade later, they’d be planning Camilla’s own funeral. Diagnosed with late-stage Hodgkin’s lymphoma just after her 20th birthday, she was given an 80% chance of survival, but the other 20% made her investigate her local undertakers (“dated, impersonal and expensive”) and work out what she wanted at her funeral (“spag bol and quite a lot of Michael Jackson”). Navigating “shit wigs” and people’s awkwardness around the subject of dying, she says that she spent a lot of time “bargaining with God”, promising that if she made it through, she’d live life to the full and appreciate every single day.

highlights.title: The sexy AI-powered dating app scams are here
highlights.summary: Security researcher Matthew "Zigula" Gore-Kormanik was analyzing a fraudulent dating app called Dora when he got a pop-up message saying he was receiving a call from Jennifer. According to her bio, she's a 41-year-old Sagittarius with red hair, blue eyes, and piercings.
body: Gore-Kormanik answered the call, but didn’t see Jennifer in his video feed. He saw a tapestry that was moving, probably due to a fan, and heard weird distortion in the background. After the call ended, “Jennifer” messaged him to say she’d had fun and “your voice is way better than expected.” His microphone hadn’t even been connected.

Gore-Kormanik was poking around Dora, and other similar apps, because I’d shared with him a spreadsheet of potential dating scam apps. I was looking into this because on June 5th, Anthropic did something uncharacteristic: The normally tight-lipped company let its threat intelligence researcher Chris Cronbaugh give a talk at a public cybersecurity conference called Sleuthcon. The company had uncovered a fraudulent dating app network after noticing unusual activity on Claude: a prepaid account sending out over 100,000 API requests per day.

highlights.summary: Explore new AI-powered advertising experiences from OpenAI, including Sponsored Agents, tools for marketers, and integrations with HubSpot and Shopify.
body: Today, we’re introducing new AI-powered experiences to make ads more useful for people and advertising easier for businesses.

We’re testing Sponsored Agents, which let people start a conversation with a business-sponsored agent after clicking an ad in ChatGPT. We are making it easier to create ads by simply writing a few prompts in ChatGPT Work. At the same time, we are making Ads Manager more powerful with new AI creative tools. Finally, new integrations with HubSpot, our first CRM partner, and Shopify, our first ecommerce partner, are bringing ChatGPT Ads into the tools businesses already use.
Together, these updates represent the next step in building our AI-based advertising platform.

Ads in ChatGPT help people find what they’re looking for or discover something they hadn’t considered. But seeing an interesting product or service is often just the beginning. A shopper might be curious about a dining table they see in an ad but have questions about whether it fits their space, how many people it seats, or how to care for its finish.

highlights.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Surpasses Star Wars: The Force Awakens to Become North America's Highest-Grossing Movie of All Time
highlights.summary: Spider-Man: Brand New Day has overtaken Star Wars: The Force Awakens to become the highest-grossing movie of all time in North America. Domestic box office for the Tom Holland sequel is now up to $936.773 million, according to Variety.
body: Of course, The Force Awakens came out 11 years ago, so there’s inflation to consider here. But Sony and Marvel owner Disney won’t care; Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been an astonishing success, so much so that even movie executives were taken by surprise.
Earlier this month, Sony Pictures chief Tom Rothman said that Brand New Day’s popularity was down to the fact that it is, essentially, a movie about “a lonely guy.”

If you’re one of the few who hasn’t seen Brand New Day yet, it picks up years after the events of 2021’s No Way Home, and shows Peter Parker struggling to cope with the absence of his friends and loved ones following Doctor Strange’s memory wipe spell. A decent chunk of the first act of the movie is spent showing Parker’s inner turmoil and, yes, his extreme loneliness, which is fueled by the end of his relationship with Zendaya’s MJ.

highlights.title: Building the materials foundation for AI
highlights.summary: The AI boom is becoming a materials challenge. As AI pushes computing into new territory, the materials behind that infrastructure are becoming just as crucial as the algorithms running on it.
body: For Mike Finelli, chief technology and innovation officer and chief North America officer at Syensqo, that convergence is transforming what advanced materials can enable. “AI is now, from a material standpoint, really pushing semiconductors and the data centers to their physical limits,” he says.

As requirements accumulate, including high temperature, purity, electrical performance, chemical resistance, plasma resistance, and long-term stability, materials move toward what Finelli calls the “top of the pyramid.” Beyond supporting AI innovation, he contends that advanced materials are “actually increasingly defining what’s going to be possible.”

That challenge is playing out across the infrastructure powering the AI surge. Syensqo is developing materials for high-voltage data center architectures, advanced sealing materials for semiconductor manufacturing, and thermal-management solutions including fluids for direct immersion cooling. Some of those innovations can also cross industry boundaries. Materials developed for electric vehicles, for example, can help address the higher voltage and energy-density demands that are emerging in data centers.
points: The AI boom is becoming a materials challenge.
As AI pushes computing into new territory, the materials behind that infrastructure are becoming just as crucial as the algorithms running on it.
For Mike Finelli, chief technology and innovation officer and chief North America officer at Syensqo, that convergence is transforming what advanced materials can enable.

highlights.title: China Isn’t Buying Silicon Valley’s Call for an AI Slowdown
highlights.summary: The US and China agree that advanced AI poses serious risks. But Beijing is deeply skeptical of a deal that prioritizes keeping US companies ahead.
body: For years, many of the most powerful people in Silicon Valley have argued that the US is locked in an AI arms race with China, and that the consequences of losing would be disastrous. But over the past week, those same executives have started emphasizing a different message. AI has the potential to become so dangerous, tech leaders say, that the two countries urgently need to work together to slow the race down.

“Global pacing will require cooperation with China, the autocratic country with by far the most advanced AI capabilities,” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei wrote in a blog post published Saturday titled “ We Must Pace the Frontier.”

China’s government and AI companies have made it clear that they’re deeply skeptical of Amodei’s proposal, but not because they want to keep blindly racing ahead or don’t believe the technology poses serious risks. The problem the Chinese government and Chinese AI companies see is far simpler. They think they’re being offered a bad deal.

highlights.title: Why Would Fashion Ever Ban Sheep Wool?
highlights.summary: Having moved the needle on fur and leather, Peta protestors are now calling on fashion to phase out sheep wool from clothing. But questions remain over whether the industry could — and should — do so.
body: It’s a complicated question. Animal rights activists argue that even the strictest certifications can’t stamp out rough handling and inhumane conditions entirely. But, unlike virgin animal fur and leather, the conversation around banning wool is nearly non-existent. In fact, knitwear is booming. And the International Woolmark Prize — which encourages emerging designers to explore the creative potential of Australian wool — is one of fashion’s leading talent incubators, counting Jean Paul Gaultier creative director Duran Lantink as its most recent winner and Karl Lagerfeld, Valentino Garavani and Yves Saint Laurent among its earliest (Woolmark does not comment on Peta activations).

highlights.title: Knight of the Seven Kingdoms Season 2 Release Window Officially Confirmed by HBO
highlights.summary: With the first season of A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms and the third season of House of the Dragon airing this year, Game of Thrones fans could potentially be left out in the cold in 2027.
body: Talking to Deadline following a successful night at the Emmys, HBO boss Casey Bloys shared updates on several of the company's shows. That included A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms. Bloys shared that the much-anticipated second season "is coming out in the first half of 2027." Since the show premiered in January 2026, that means the time between seasons will be a year and a half at most, which isn't actually that bad in the current prestige television landscape.

It is also faster than House of the Dragon, which has had two years between seasons so farz. Game of Thrones used to release a season a year (except for the two-year wait for the final season), so it's nice that A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms is getting back to that cadence. House of the Dragon is set to start shooting season 4 next spring, meaning it likely won't release until 2028.

The first season of the prequel series adapted the entirety of George R.R. Martin's 1998 novella The Hedge Knight. The second season will adapt The Sworn Sword, the second novella about the adventures of Ser Dunk the Tall and his squire Egg, who is revealed to be Westeros' king-to-be Aegon Targaryen V.
